page_story_title: The GUTSKI story | Ski pullovers from Limburg
page_story_desc: From a sports shop in Kerkrade to the slopes of the Alps: the story behind GUTSKI's knitted ski pullovers.
st_p1: GUTSKI was born on the shop floor of a sports store in Kerkrade, in the south of the Netherlands. For years we saw the same thing: winter sports fans looking for a ski pullover with character — something you won't find on the rack at every chain store. So we started making them ourselves.
st_p2: Every GUTSKI ski pullover is a knitted sweater with a story of its own. Designs like Wir sind Spitze, Platzhirsch and Flying Hirsch nod to the après-ski, but are made to be worn on the slopes too: warm, breathable and built to last. From the first sketch to the final knit pattern, everything happens in-house.
st_p3: Want something entirely your own? With our 3D configurator you design your own ski pullover — colours, text and motif — and see the result instantly.
st_p4: You'll find GUTSKI online at Skipullies.com and at our stockists in the Netherlands, Germany and Austria.

page_material_title: What a GUTSKI ski pullover is made of | GUTSKI
page_material_desc: What's a GUTSKI ski pullover made of? 92% polyester, 8% spandex and a brushed interior that keeps you warm on the slopes and fresh at the bar.
mat_intro: A ski pullover you wear all day needs to do more than look good in photos. That's why we chose a fabric that performs on the slopes and still feels fresh at the bar.
mat_s1_h: What a GUTSKI is made of
mat_s1_p: Every GUTSKI ski pullover is knitted from 92% polyester and 8% spandex, with a brushed interior weighing 220–230 gsm. That weight gives the pully enough substance to stay warm without feeling bulky, and the brushed interior adds a soft layer against your skin.
mat_s2_h: Warm on the slopes, fresh at the bar
mat_s2_p: The fabric retains body warmth when it's cold and wicks away sweat the moment you start moving. That means you can go from a run down the mountain to the terrace without the pully feeling damp. An antibacterial finish keeps it fresh, even if you wear it all day — or for several days on a ski trip.
mat_s3_p: Thanks to 4-way stretch, the fabric moves with you in every direction. Handy for a full day of carving turns, and just as handy on the dance floor of the après-ski bar later.
mat_s4_p: Curious how this fabric looks in your own design? The 3D configurator at skipullies.com shows you instantly how colour, text and motif come together on this material.

page_pully_title: Ski pullover vs. regular sweater: the difference
page_pully_desc: A ski pullover looks like a sweater, but it's built to move, stay warm and stay on all day — from the slopes to the après-ski bar.
pl_h1: What makes a ski pullover different from a regular sweater
pl_intro: At first glance, a ski pullover looks like a thick sweater with a fun pattern. The difference isn't in how it looks — it's in what it needs to do.
pl_s1_p: A regular sweater is knitted to sit still. A GUTSKI ski pullover is knitted from 92% polyester and 8% spandex with 4-way stretch, so the fabric moves with every turn you make instead of bouncing back or pulling tight.
pl_s2_h: Stays warm, even when you sweat
pl_s2_p: Cotton and regular wool hold onto moisture and get damp fast. The brushed interior of a GUTSKI (220–230 gsm) does the opposite: it retains body warmth and wicks sweat away the moment you start moving. That keeps you warm on the chairlift and dry after a run.
pl_s3_h: One pully, from slopes to bar
pl_s3_p: You take off a regular sweater the moment you start being active. A ski pullover is designed to stay on — from the first lift in the morning to the last round at the bar at night. The antibacterial finish helps keep it fresh, even after a full day.
pl_s4_p: Where a regular sweater is often plain, a GUTSKI is designed to stand out — with designs that nod to the après-ski scene, like Wir sind Spitze and Platzhirsch. Exactly the kind of sweater that makes your group, team or friend crew instantly recognisable.
